about: How the product's screens, menus and content relate: which screens exist, what the menus hold and where each item goes, what the top bar does, which control on which screen leads to which other screen and what it carries along, and which part of docs/SCREEN_DATA_MAP.md says where each screen's content comes from. Read it BEFORE you build a menu or a screen from a picture: a picture shows the words in a menu and not where they lead. tools/gui_checks/check_navigation.py checks it (and, with --prototype, checks it against the prototype's source); docs/NAVIGATION_MAP.md is generated from it. Everything here is made up: the sample project is invented.

notes: A screen's name (the menu label, the breadcrumb, the document title) is not always the heading inside the screen. Read from the running prototype's sample project: nine screens repeat their name as the heading; Home's heading is a sentence with a count taken from the data; the Review queue's is the name of the cluster showing; The V's is 'The engineering V'. A rebuild puts the name in the menu, the breadcrumb and the title, and lets the heading be what the screen needs. Do not take a screen's name from its heading in a picture.
A screen's content is described by its data_map sections in docs/SCREEN_DATA_MAP.md. A menu item's words are STATIC; only the count on 'Review queue' is data.
'from' was read from the code by one agent: the checks confirm which screens each piece of code can lead to, not which screen that code is shown on.

In the prototype a menu item changes only which screen shows. A cluster selected or a filter set earlier is still set when you come back to that screen (read from the code, not run). Say in your report if you keep or clear that state differently.
